newsitem.title: USA: Chase sees credit card chargeoffs peaking.
newsitem.headline: Chase sees credit card chargeoffs peaking.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp Chief Financial Officer Peter Tobin said Tuesday the bank expects credit card charge-offs, which reached $358 million in the first quarter, to peak in the second quarter before declining in the second half of the year.

Speaking during a conference call after the bank released its earnings for the first quarter, Tobin added that he expected credit card charge-offs for the entire year to be about 5.6 percent of average managed receivables for the year.
Those numbers were good in comparison to other major lenders, he added.

Tobin also said the bank was on track to realize the cost savings it projected when it merged with Chemical Banking Corp. The bank had projected savings of between $630 million and $680 million in 1997.
"We're on target for that," he said, adding that the bank would save between $140 million and $150 million per quarter this year.
Tobin said that Chase would concentrate on building its securities business from within, although he said that "down the road" the bank might consider a boutique acquisition of some sort.
